questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The shop opens at eight o'clock every day.
The shop open at eight o'clock every day.
The shop opening at eight o'clock every day.
The shop is open at eight o'clock every day as a habit.
questions.explanation: A daily habit uses the present simple, and with 'the shop' (it) the verb takes -s: 'opens'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'a person who travels to visit places for pleasure'?
questions.explanation: A 'tourist' travels to see and enjoy new places; the other words describe different jobs.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The Blue Nile is ______ than the small river near our school.'
questions.explanation: Short adjectives add -er and use 'than' to compare two things: 'wider than'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence asking for permission politely.
options: May I leave the room, please?
May I to leave the room, please?
May I leaving the room, please?
May I leaves the room, please?
questions.explanation: After the modal 'may', use the base verb with no 'to': 'May I leave...?'

questions.prompt: What does 'hygiene' mean?
options: A type of medicine for fever
Keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy
A serious illness of the lungs
A plan for spending money wisely
questions.explanation: 'Hygiene' means keeping clean to prevent illness, such as washing your hands.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She has took the medicine already.
She has taken the medicine already.
She have taken the medicine already.
She has taked the medicine already.
questions.explanation: Use 'has' + the past participle 'taken' (take - took - taken): 'She has taken'.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive: 'Volunteers plant thousands of trees each year.'
options: Thousands of trees plant each year.
Thousands of trees are planted each year.
Thousands of trees is planted each year.
Thousands of trees were planted each year.
questions.explanation: Present passive uses am/is/are + past participle; 'trees' is plural, so 'are planted'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If the road is repaired, the journey ______ much shorter.'
questions.explanation: The result clause of the first conditional uses 'will' + base verb: 'will be'.

questions.prompt: "There is no milk left." Which reply shows a decision made at that moment?
options: I am going to the shop later as planned.
I will buy some on my way home.
I buy some on my way home.
I am buying some at four o'clock.
questions.explanation: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses 'will': 'I will buy some'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'There is only ______ bread left, so share it carefully.'
questions.explanation: 'Bread' is uncountable, so a small amount is 'a little': 'a little bread'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'February is the ______ month of the year.'
questions.explanation: Short adjectives form the superlative with 'the' + -est: 'the shortest'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses a strong obligation that comes from an outside rule?
options: You have to wear a seatbelt; it is the law.
questions.explanation: 'Have to' shows an obligation from an outside rule or law; 'should' would be only advice.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'an ability to do something well, learned through practice'?
questions.explanation: A 'skill' is an ability gained through practice, such as typing or driving.

questions.prompt: Combine: 'This is the phone. I bought it last month.' Best combined sentence:
options: This is the phone which I bought it last month.
This is the phone that I bought last month.
This is the phone where I bought last month.
This is the phone who I bought last month.
questions.explanation: Use 'that' (or 'which') for a thing, and do not repeat 'it': 'the phone that I bought last month'.

questions.prompt: Choose the most natural sentence for a fixed plan with a time.
options: We meet the supplier at noon on Thursday.
We are meeting the supplier at noon on Thursday.
We will meeting the supplier at noon on Thursday.
We going to meet the supplier at noon on Thursday.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is natural for fixed arrangements with a time: 'We are meeting the supplier at noon on Thursday'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The witness gave a detailed and accurate account of the accident.' The word 'accurate' means...
questions.explanation: 'Accurate' means correct and exact, which fits a reliable account of events.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: 'The new bridge will ______ the two villages.'
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence or have an impact on; 'effect' is usually a noun.

questions.prompt: Report this sentence: He said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
options: He said that he will call me the next day.
He said that he would call me the next day.
He said that he would call you the next day.
He said that he will call you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'will' shifts to 'would' and 'you' becomes 'me': 'he would call me the next day'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I knew her number, I will phone her.
If I knew her number, I would phone her.
If I would know her number, I phoned her.
If I know her number, I would phone her.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: 'If' + past simple, 'would' + base verb, so 'If I knew..., I would phone'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive sentence for: 'Someone is cleaning the classroom now.'
options: The classroom is being cleaned now.
The classroom was being cleaned now.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive is 'is/are being + past participle': 'is being cleaned'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: She avoided to answer the question.
questions.explanation: The verb 'avoid' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'avoided answering'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The list of names are on the desk.
The list of names is on the desk.
The list of names were on the desk.
The list of names being on the desk.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'list', not 'names', so the verb is singular: 'The list ... is on the desk'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag: 'Let's start the meeting, ______?'
questions.explanation: A suggestion beginning with 'Let's' always takes the tag 'shall we?'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'The success of the harvest depends ______ enough rain.'
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'depend on something': 'depends on enough rain'.

questions.prompt: Choose the best linking word: 'She spoke quietly ______ the baby would not wake up.'
questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose: she spoke quietly with the aim of not waking the baby.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct word form: 'The scientists made an important ______ about the new medicine.'
questions.explanation: After 'an important' a noun is needed: 'discovery'.

questions.prompt: Choose the best phrasal verb: 'I don't know this word, so I will ______ it ______ in a dictionary.'
questions.explanation: 'Look up' means to find information in a reference book, such as a word in a dictionary.

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to 'fragile'?
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means delicate and easily broken, like glass.

questions.prompt: Which word means the opposite of 'patient'?
questions.explanation: Before words starting with 'p', the negative prefix is usually 'im-', giving 'impatient'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He waited for hour before the bus came.
He waited for a hour before the bus came.
He waited for an hour before the bus came.
He waited for the hour before the bus came.
questions.explanation: 'Hour' begins with a silent 'h', so the vowel sound takes 'an': 'an hour'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: 'The weather had a serious ______ on the crops this season.'
questions.explanation: Here a noun meaning 'result' is needed, so 'effect' is correct; 'affect' is the verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct and consistent tenses.
options: She had finished her homework before her father comes home.
She finished her homework before her father had come home.
She had finished her homework before her father came home.
She finishes her homework before her father came home.
questions.explanation: The earlier action uses the past perfect ('had finished') before the later past action ('came home').

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about an unreal past situation.
options: If we had saved more, we could buy the land.
If we saved more, we could have bought the land.
If we had saved more, we could have bought the land.
If we would have saved more, we had bought the land.
questions.explanation: The third conditional uses 'If' + past perfect and 'would/could have' + past participle: 'had saved ... could have bought'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'No sooner had the guests sat down than the lights went out.' What does this tell us?
options: The lights went out long after the guests sat down.
The lights went out just after the guests sat down.
The lights stayed on the whole evening.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner had X happened than Y' means Y followed almost immediately after X.

questions.prompt: Read: 'The plan looks promising on paper, but it remains to be seen whether it can work in practice.' What is the writer's attitude?
options: Completely certain the plan will succeed
Cautious; not yet convinced it will work
Sure the plan has already failed
questions.explanation: 'Remains to be seen' shows the writer is cautious and is waiting for proof before judging.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Thanks a lot,' he said flatly, looking at the broken chair he had just been given. What is his real attitude?
options: He is truly grateful for the gift.
He is displeased; he is being sarcastic.
He is excited to fix the chair.
He is surprised by a wonderful present.
questions.explanation: Speaking 'flatly' about a broken chair contradicts the words of thanks, signalling sarcasm and displeasure.
